body.x: Curinginnos. Inc. (CEO Kweon Yechan) participated in the 'Startup Zone' at the Eureka Park K-STARTUP integrated hall of 'CES 2023' in Las Vegas, USA from January 5 (Thursday) to 8 (Sunday, local time) for a total of 4 days.

Curinginnos is creating an exercise partner robot system that allows people to freely and systematically enjoy exercise with people around the world without being constrained by time and number of people, based on the slogan of ‘Connect One, Together Even When Alone’.

‘iVOLVE Trainer’, introduced at the trade show, is an AI 1-man personalized tennis robot system capable of dynamic and fun tennis training, games, and remote matches and games. It collects user data and analyzes exercise patterns and strengths and weaknesses and uses this as a base to provide training programs and user competition programs through an autonomous tennis robot system that moves and executes the program like real people.

Kweon Yechan, the CEO of Curinginnos, explained that, “Serving as the vice-chair of my university tennis club and as a soldier in charge of managing tennis during my time in the Korean army, I’ve seen many people quit due to high coaching costs, lacking management systems, and absence of partners. This isn’t limited to just Korea and is a phenomenon occurring in all tennis societies. As such, we developed the iVOLVE system so that people can systematically and freely enjoy tennis even when alone.”

Currently, iVOLVE systems have the achievements of being sent to numerous famous tennis academies. Based on the accomplishments made in Korea, Curinginnos aims to provide innovative services to all tennis enthusiasts around the world.

The ‘iVOLVE Standard’ product, an ICT tennis ball machine, has been officially launched in Korea and is on sale in the market, while the ‘iVOLVE Pro’ product, an autonomous tennis ball machine, currently has MVP development and self-driving algorithm development completed and is scheduled to be officially launched in the US in the 3rd quarter of 2023. The ‘iVOLVE Eyes’, an unmanned referee and match evaluation system, also had the development of all the algorithms completed, and is undergoing field tests with the goal of an official launch in the US market by the 3rd quarter of 2023.
CEO Kweon Yechan said that, “We hope to show off the excellence of the iVOLVE tennis partner robot system at CES and secure the cooperation of global buyers and investors.”

‘CES’ is the world’s biggest IT trade show and is a place where one can see the direction and trends of the appliance industry of the entire world. Hosted by the Consumer Technology Association (CTA), it is held annually in Las Vegas, USA in January. Having reported on CES for 17 consecutive years, AVING News started reporting news of CES to the entire world since 2006, and conducted ‘BEST OF CES’, which chose the most innovative product and technology, and ‘BEST OF MADE IN KOREA, which chose the best innovative company in Korea. In addition, it vividly relayed on-site issues in CES through ‘AVING LIVE’.

The K-STARTUP Joint Pavilion featured joint participation of institutions like the Korea Institute of Startup & Entrepreneurship Development, Seoul Business Agency, and Seoul Digital Foundation, as well as 51 Korean innovative companies, to enter the US market and discover global partners. In addition, university student supporters of CES 2023 chosen by each university (Kyunghee, Kookmin, Sogang, Chung-Ang) matched to participating companies based on their respective majors and fields of business.
